prompt: Write two generic static methods on ListUtils: swap exchanges the elements at two indexes, and reverseInPlace reverses the whole list by calling swap.
explanation: A generic method declares its own type parameter (<T>) right before the return type, so it works on a List of any element type while staying type-safe: the value you get out can be set back in. swap needs a temp variable of type T to avoid losing one element. reverseInPlace shows how a small generic helper composes into a bigger algorithm: two indexes close in from the ends, swapping as they go.
hints: In swap, store list.get(i) in a variable of type T before overwriting index i.
list.set(index, value) replaces an element and is all you need besides get.
For reverseInPlace, use two counters: left starting at 0 and right at size() - 1; swap and move them toward each other while left < right.
